# How to run DAQ with dream: 

On banco computer HV remote control : VNC viewer : IP address: ? password: ? 

For data taking: 

ssh banco@IP (pass: banco) 

In the directory: /local/home/banco/DAQ\_Control\_Dream\_Beam/

Instructions here: https\://github.com/akallitss/DAQ\_Control\_Dream\_Beam/blob/main/README.md   

![][image1]  
Pass admin

🔗 GUI remote links

  \- From the CERN network (you're on-site): open directly —  
  http\://128.141.21.144:5001 (verified reachable from lxplus)  
  \- From an external network: tunnel through lxplus (internet-facing, and it can reach banco):  
  ssh \-L 5001:128.141.21.144:5001 lxplus  
  \- then open http\://localhost:5001

# How to run DAQ with VMM-alinx: 

ssh \-Y username@IP

GUI to run the DAQ instructions here: [https\://github.com/akallitss/DAQ\_Control\_VMM\_Beam/blob/main/README.md](https://github.com/akallitss/DAQ_Control_VMM_Beam/blob/main/README.md) 

From cern network [http\://128.141.21.163:5002/](http://128.141.21.163:5002/) to monitor the gui and take runs

cd /local/p2/p2testbench/TestBenchCERN

Run the slow\_control software /local/p2/p2testbench/TestBenchCERN vmmdcs\_alinx &

On the slow control window, load the configuration file (start with config\_alinx\_noThresholds  
Open/Check communication to see the status of the hybrids  (?) 

Configuration: Each hybrid has 2 VMM cards, from this you can mask on the right side of the window the channels they are noisy with checking the box SM  
**\*\*\*Important each time you are masking a channel with SM you need to SEND the command to the chip before starting the run to update the configuration file.**

Status: green means listening  
	Blue means running 

I2C: check chip temperatures

On the tab DAQ and Calibration: Setting low voltage on the detectors lets say 100V D/A   
You can take data for 1000ms and see the automatic calibration of the Hybrids

It may take several iterations and for that you may need to rephrase the powersycle: 

./switchOff\_tdk.sh  
You will see sth like: 

TDKL 192.168.0.249 is now OFF.  
TDKL 192.168.0.248 is now OFF.  
TDKL 192.168.0.247 is now OFF.  
2025-11-12 17:18:01.580061   TDK: 192.168.0.249 00.0032 V ; 00.0000 A  
2025-11-12 17:18:02.087657   TDK: 192.168.0.248 00.0014 V ; 00.0000 A  
2025-11-12 17:18:02.111207   TDK: 192.168.0.247 00.0012 V ; 00.0000 A

 and then   
./switchOn\_tdk.sh

You will see sth like : 

TDKL 192.168.0.249 is now OFF.  
TDKL 192.168.0.248 is now OFF.  
TDKL 192.168.0.247 is now OFF.  
TDKL 192.168.0.248 is now ON.  
TDKL 192.168.0.247 is now ON.  
Namespace(state='Off', time\_out=1.0, verbose=1)  
aurduinoSerial.is\_open True  
Main: aurduinoSerial.write OK with state Low  
Main: State change OK : sent \=  Low  received \=  Low  
aurduinoSerial.is\_open False  
Namespace(state='On', time\_out=1.0, verbose=1)  
aurduinoSerial.is\_open True  
Main: aurduinoSerial.write OK with state High  
Main: State change OK : sent \=  High  received \=  High  
aurduinoSerial.is\_open False  
TDKL 192.168.0.249 is now ON.  
2025-11-12 17:18:19.330420   TDK: 192.168.0.249 11.9975 V ; 01.0491 A  
2025-11-12 17:18:19.843888   TDK: 192.168.0.248 03.3126 V ; 01.0272 A  
2025-11-12 17:18:19.867191   TDK: 192.168.0.247 02.1932 V ; 06.6537 A

Repeat the calibration to see the hybrid status, if needed, you can mask the dead channels from the measurements, and continue with sending the config to the chip and move on to take data. 

Data taking: 

Once ssh on the machine run : tmux ls to see the available windows   
Go to:  tmux a \-t daq   
./daq\_control status to see the status of the daq  
./daq\_control.sh start \<run\_number\>

Were to find the data : /local/p2/p2data/cern\_202511/\<run\_number\>   
Binary files and decoded root files are generated automatically

**Run 16** drift\_transparency\_1 

— first points above drift gap 450 V

  2026-07-27 20:05:33 → 20:47:00 · 6 × \~6 min · 9.5 M triggers · 26 GB

  Run in the last hour before the 21:00 access. HV powered off and verified at the crate at 20:49 (all 10 channels power \= 0, vmon \= 0.00).

  \- Motivation: every drift curve in the campaign was truncated at gap 450 V — not physics, but the 900 V drift ceiling (at the operating mesh of 450, gap 450 is the arithmetic maximum), and  
  the overnight 2D grid applied that same cap to every mesh row. Dropping the mesh to 390 buys 60 V of new gap and lowers the amplification field, pulling the expected transparency turnover  
  into reach. Mesh 390 already had a full curve (gaps 150–450) in drift\_mesh\_2d\_2, so these points extend a measured curve.  
  \- Points on MID+OUT, mesh fixed 390, anchors first and last (mean index 2.5 of 5 — dead centre, so a linear drift cancels and the anchor pair measures it):

  | sub-run      | drift (gap) |  triggers | MID h/t · amp | OUT h/t · amp |  
  |--------------|-------------|-----------|---------------|---------------|  
  | tr\_00 anchor | 840 (450)   | 1 673 636 | 0.929 · 62    | 1.104 · 85    |  
  | tr\_01        | 860 (470)   | 1 128 260 | 0.922 · 61    | 1.097 · 84    |  
  | tr\_02        | 875 (485)   | 1 681 695 | 0.913 · 61    | 1.095 · 84    |  
  | tr\_03        | 890 (500)   | 1 670 974 | 0.908 · 60    | 1.095 · 83    |  
  | tr\_04        | 900 (510)   | 1 633 383 | 0.903 · 60    | 1.085 · 82    |  
  | tr\_05 anchor | 840 (450)   | 1 677 925 | 0.934 · 62    | 1.100 · 85    |

  \- Gaps 470/485/500/510 are new to the campaign.  
  \- Result: from gap 450 → 510, MID −2.8 %, OUT −1.7 %, median amplitude −3 % on both; anchors reproduce to \+0.5 % / −0.4 %. The trend is several times the reproducibility and is real, but  
  it is a slow decline, not a turnover knee — the plateau at mesh 390 extends past gap 510, so the maximum is still not bracketed. Reaching it needs a lower mesh (370/350, where  
  drift\_mesh\_2d\_2 already has curves) or a drift ceiling above 900 V.  
  \- ⚠ P2\_OUT is discharging occasionally at high drift field: medians clean (0.003–0.005 µA, no trips), but sporadic mesh excursions grow with field — max 0.20 µA at gap 450 → 0.22 → 0.30 →  
  0.47 µA at gap 500 — and the closing anchor returned at 0.25 µA vs 0.20 µA for the opening one at the identical setpoint. Still \~4× below the 2 µA alarm, but the two anchors are not in the  
  same state, so the bracket correction is not purely linear drift. (The gap-510 maximum reads low only because the excursions are sporadic; not a recovery.)

## Saturday 25 / 7 / 26

The VMM-based electronics with 10 frontend Hybrids is up.  
9 Hybrids with IDs from 1 to 9 are waiting to be connected to the detectors.  
1 Hybrid with ID 0 is used to digitize the external trigger.

## On Trigger signal digitization:

The external trigger signal is provided by the setup from the INFN Roma group.  
It is fed to a CAEN NIM fanout module.  
The copies of the Trigger are sent to:

1) The TCM module of the Dream/FEU electronics  
2) A NIM scaler  
3) To the Hybrid 0 of the VMM-based electronics

The NIM fanout module is from an old generation.  
It is configured as 4-Or-ed input to 8 output fanout.  
There are 2 groups of 4 outputs.  
And 2 outputs in each 4 groups share the same NIM driver.  
A NIM driver provides 32 mA current creating \-1.6V signal on a 50 Ohm terminated input.  
If another output of a 2-output group is also used the resulting signal is \-0.8V (25 mA x 25 Ohm).  
This is weird but OK, should not prevent VMMs from digitizing the trigger signal.

However, the behaviour of the Trigger Hybrid 0 is even more weird.  
The only channel that currently correctly digitizes the trigger is channel 60 on VMM 1\.  
It produces strong ADC values of about 1000 ADC bins when plugged in a particular output of the fanout.  
When the Trigger signal is provided from the neighbour output of the same 2-output group the ADC values are about 700\.  
The channel 60 of the VMM 1 counts the triggers consistently with the triggers counted by the TCM in “normal” non-too-high rate runs.  
The trigger rate is about 26-30 kHz.  
(It is to be noted that other groups need quite some “gymnastics” to get the trigger rate in kHz from their measurements. But at least, they manage to take data with VMMs. We’ll see what will happen with us)

We had a channel 40 on the same VMM 1 that was working fine and was producing ADC values of about 1000 bins.  
But after some software reconfiguration the ADC counts started to be about 400 and we never could recover the initial values.  
The channels 0 and 20 of the same VMM 1 \- all easily available on the frontend panel of the trigger Hybrid are even more weird.

All attempts to digitize the trigger signal with the VMM 0 of the trigger Hybrid 0 were fiasco.

Currently, VMM0 global discriminator threshold is set to max DAC 1023 value.  
This prevents its channels from counting.  
The VMM1 global discriminator threshold is set to 512 DAC value and the channels 0, 20 and 40 are masked.

The correct digitization of the trigger by the channel 60 of the VMM1 has been validated by the 8.2 kHz NIM signal generator and the external INFN Roma NIM trigger.

All this is very puzzling.  
One of the explanations can be a bad common grounding of the racks with VMM electronics and with the NIM crate hosting the fanout.  
We may need to unify the ground of the two racks by a copper braid.

## On data taking

A “durty” python script has been developed to:

1) Reset VMM-based system and place all Hybrids in aligned and ready for acquisition state  
2) Configure the system with the default base configuration settings from yaml file and from a text file exceptions from the default configuration (SFM, global threshold, channel mask, etc)  
3) Run acquisition for a certain time optionally with tshark monitoring or dumpcap data saving \- both either as a one shot or periodic data production

The script is under the /local/p2/p2testbench/TestBenchCosmic directory.  
It is called something like:  
p2basket\_ExtConfig\_v0.py \- the version for Maarten doing a), b) and partially c)  
p2basket\_ExtConfig\_work.py \- the version under development and to be cleaned  
(It is clear that the script is kind of “fourre-tout” and probably needs to be split into 3 utilities.)

The script has been used for an overnight run of 8 hours with the following configuration:  
The channel 35 of the 2 VMMs of all Hybrids from 1 to 9 was internally pulsed.  
The channel 60 of the VMM 1 of the Hybrid 0 was digitizing the Trigger signal.  
The run was monitored by the tshark logging an activity line every 20 sec.  
The run went fine without problems.  
The internal pulser produces about 11 kHz hits on a channel.  
With 18 active channels (9 hybrids, 2 VMM/Hybrid, 1 channel / VMM) the rate overall rate should be 192 kHz.  
Exactly what is recorded by tshark during out-of-spill periods.  
During the spill periods there is the trigger activity that can do up to 25-30 kHz.  
This is seen by tshark with the hit rate recorded of about 220 kHz.

This is an “Encouraging” result, but…  
When testing the system with frequent start-stops of acquisition, the data output from the Alinx backend to the control PC can freeze.  
To revive the system the “warm reset” procedure has to be applied.  
The script does this fine bringing the system to the ready state, but we need to find the reason:

1) Why the communication over the 10 GE interface stacks time-to-time  
2) Why some of the hybrids may emerge in a non-ready state and need an extra warm reset

# Thursday 30 / 07 / 26

An attempt was made to implement the following scheme to digitize trigger signals by Hyb0.  
![][image17]

The scheme has been tested with the beam and it shows flaws.  
The Dream électronics processes the muon trigger at \~29 kHz rate.  
This corresponds well to the rate given by the “Unconstraint trigger scaler”.  
The “Constraint trigger scaler” shows about 2 kHz rate.  
Meaning the veto scheme is wrong.  
This will be debugged during the next long access \- may be this evening or tomorrow morning.  
(Benjamin brought dual timers that can be used to generate high rate triggers for debugging.)

When the busy signal is removed from the Veto unit both scalers show the same rate.  
And the Hybrid 0 shows about 55-60 kHz rate with wireshark monitoring.

The configuration of the Hybrid 0 is as follows:

1) Gain (sg) : 1mV/fC  
2) Peaking time (st) : 25 ns  
3) Global threshold (sdt) : 428 DAC units  
4) Fast recovery (srec) : 0 (off)

The constraint trigger signal width is set to 150 ns by the adjustment potentiometer of the Veto unit.  
Both channels on Hybrid 0, Vmm0 44 and Vmm1 20, give ADC bins of \~940.  
(The small afterglow counts of \< 100 ADC bins are suppressed by the high global threshold).
